auth.setupSubtitle: Create the administrator account. You will use it to log in from now on.
auth.usernameHint: 3–64 characters: letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.
auth.keyHint: X-TOOLS generated a secret key in its data directory (secret.key). Stored credentials can only be decrypted with it – include it in your backups.
auth.setupCodeHint: Printed in the server log: docker logs x-tools
auth.codeSubtitle: Enter the code from your authenticator app.
auth.codeHint: 6 digits – or one of your recovery codes

servers.moreText: Servers at home (e.g. Proxmox) report through a small agent – outbound only, no open ports.
servers.noSnapshotLong: No Docker data yet. The collector container (x-tools-collector) writes it within a minute after starting.
servers.stale: The Docker data is outdated (last update {{when}}). Is the x-tools-collector container running?
servers.agentPending: The agent is created but has not sent any data yet.

docker.listedHint: A service with this folder is in the services list
docker.maskedNote: Passwords, tokens and keys in these files are masked (••••••). .env files are never read.
docker.protectedHint: X-TOOLS itself – cannot be stopped from here
docker.readonlyNote: This agent only reports – switch on “Allow control” with a new install command to control containers here.

overview.notifyOn: You will be notified about new problems.
overview.start2: Add customers and assign their sites
overview.start4: Connect more servers with an agent

sites.title: Website checks
sites.notChecked: Not checked yet – runs every 5 minutes.

notify.enabledHint: Send a message when something needs attention.
notify.delayHint: Only report problems that last at least this long.
notify.recoveryHint: Also notify when a problem is solved
notify.tokenStored: Stored – leave empty to keep it
notify.chatIdHint: Your user ID, a group ID (-100…) or @channel
notify.noBaseUrl: Tip: set XT_BASE_URL so notifications contain a link to X-TOOLS.

agents.intro: Agents report other servers to X-TOOLS – outbound only, they never receive commands. Install one on the Proxmox host and one on every LXC/VM that runs Docker.
agents.name: Name
agents.keyOnce: Copy the key now – it is shown only once. Only a hash is stored.
agents.step4: Behind Cloudflare Access: add a service token and a “Service Auth” rule for /api/agent/report (see Help).
agents.proxmoxHint: Also report nodes, storage, LXCs and VMs through the Proxmox API (read-only).
agents.proxmoxUrlHint: Seen from the Proxmox host – usually https://127.0.0.1:8006
agents.verifyTls: Verify the TLS certificate (off for the default self-signed certificate)
agents.proxmoxHowto: Proxmox: Datacenter → Permissions → API Tokens → Add; then Permissions → Add → API Token Permission, path /, role PVEAuditor (read-only) – for control a role with VM.PowerMgmt too, e.g. PVEVMUser. The secret only goes into the install command.
agents.cfHint: Service token so the agent gets through (rule: Service Auth for /api/agent/).
agents.composeRootsHint: Where to look for compose files on that server (comma-separated)
agents.reinstallNote: This creates a new key. The agent installed so far stops reporting until you run the new command.
agents.runThis: Run this on the server, as root
agents.runThisHint: On Proxmox you are root in the shell; elsewhere replace “| sh” with “| sudo sh”.
agents.fact1: Works once and only for one hour.
agents.fact2: Installs the systemd service x-tools-agent (Python 3.10+, nothing else) – read-only, no open ports.
agents.fact3: The server shows up under Servers within a minute.
agents.dockerAltHint: Use deploy/agent from the repository with this .env (the key is shown only now):

kinds.proxmoxHint: Host metrics, nodes, storage and all LXCs/VMs via the Proxmox API (read-only token).
kinds.dockerHint: A server, LXC or VM with Docker: containers, compose files, git status.

agents.removedText: X-TOOLS no longer accepts reports from this agent. To remove it from {{host}} as well, run this there:
agents.uninstallHint: Removes the systemd service and its files, or the Docker container – whichever is installed.
agents.uninstallNote: Without it the agent keeps trying to report and is rejected. Later you can also find the command under Help → Agents.
agents.updateHint: A newer agent is available: create a new install command and run it on the server.
agents.controlHintDocker: Operators can start, stop and restart containers on this server and read their logs. Off: the agent only reports.
agents.controlHintProxmox: Operators can start, shut down, stop and reboot LXCs/VMs. The API token then needs VM.PowerMgmt (see the hint above).

about.keyEnv: The secret key comes from XT_SECRET_KEY – keep a copy of it.
about.keyFile: The secret key is stored in {{dir}}/secret.key.
about.backupHint: Back up the whole data volume including the key. Without it stored credentials and tokens cannot be decrypted.
about.config: These values are set through environment variables (deploy/.env).

general.customersHint: For sites you host for others: contacts, agreements and external checks of their domains. Stored customers are kept when you switch it off.

fleet.noData: No data in the last report.

history.noMetrics: Not enough data yet – a sample is taken every 5 minutes.
history.chartLabel: Load, memory and disk over time
history.noEvents: No problems in the last {{days}} days.
history.title: Recent events

account.changed: Password changed – other sessions were logged out.
account.twoFactorText: Besides your password, log in with a code from an authenticator app (e.g. Apple Passwords, 1Password, Google Authenticator, Aegis).
account.step1: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app (or enter the key manually).
account.step2: Enter the 6-digit code it shows to confirm.
account.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app
account.recoveryText: Store these codes somewhere safe (e.g. your password manager). Each one logs you in once if you lose your phone. They are shown only now.

backup.createText: Database and secret key in one file, encrypted with a passphrase you choose. Anyone with file and passphrase can read everything in it, including credentials.
backup.passphraseHint: At least 10 characters – without it the backup cannot be restored.
backup.restoreText: Replaces everything in this installation with the backup. Everyone is logged out afterwards.
backup.confirmText: All current data is replaced by {{name}}. This cannot be undone.

users.intro: Who may log in and what they may do.
users.resetHint: The user is logged out everywhere and logs in with this password.
users.initialPasswordHint: Tell it to the user – they can change it under Settings → Account.

rolesHint.viewer: Sees everything, changes nothing – no credentials, no logs.
rolesHint.operator: Maintains services, customers and credentials, starts and stops containers.
rolesHint.admin: Everything, including users, settings, agents, backups and the audit log.

audit.intro: Who did what – kept for one year.

assistant.title: New service
assistant.sub: Pick a template – the assistant writes the configuration and a checklist.

templatesHint.webapp: A ready-made Docker image that serves HTTP.
templatesHint.node: Your code in the folder, built with a Dockerfile.
templatesHint.static: HTML/CSS/JS from a folder, served by nginx.
templatesHint.postgres: A database for your apps – not published on the web.
templatesHint.custom: Only the reverse proxy / tunnel configuration.

assistant.portHint: Free port on the host; inside the container: {{internal}}
assistant.portUsed: Port {{port}} is already used by {{by}} on this host – pick another one.

exposeHint.tunnel: No open ports; route in the tunnel.
exposeHint.caddy: Own reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS.
exposeHint.nginx: nginx with a certificate from certbot.
exposeHint.traefik: Docker labels for an existing Traefik.
exposeHint.lan: Reachable as http://<ip>:<port> in your network.

assistant.noHttp: A database is not published on the web – it listens on localhost only (or in the LAN).
assistant.storeSecrets: Save the generated passwords ({{names}}) as credentials of the service
assistant.filesIntro: Copy or download the files, put them into the folder on the server and work through the checklist.
assistant.noFiles: Nothing to generate for this choice.
assistant.envNote: Contains generated passwords – keep it private (chmod 600), never commit it.
assistant.doneSub: The service is in your list – now set it up.
assistant.doneText: Work through the checklist; you can tick off the steps in the service.
assistant.lanOnly: Reachable in the LAN as http://{{host}}:{{port}} – no proxy configuration needed.

cloudflare.partial: Some data could not be read:
cloudflare.permissionsHint: Check the permissions of the API token (Settings → Cloudflare).
cloudflare.localConfig: This tunnel is configured locally (config.yml) – its routes cannot be read through the API.
cloudflare.settingsIntro: Read-only: X-TOOLS shows your zones, DNS records, tunnels with their routes and Access applications, and checks them against your services. It never changes anything at Cloudflare.
cloudflare.step1: Cloudflare dashboard → My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → Custom token.
cloudflare.step3: Account and zone resources: the accounts/zones X-TOOLS may see. Create, copy, paste below.
cloudflare.tokenHint: Stored encrypted; only used for reading.
cloudflare.tokenReplace: A token is stored – enter a new one to replace it.
cloudflare.name: Name
cloudflare.serviceHint: Seen from the server the tunnel runs on, e.g. http://localhost:8080
cloudflare.routeDns: Point the DNS record to this tunnel (create or update the CNAME)
cloudflare.allowWriteHint: Operators can add, edit and delete DNS records and tunnel routes. The token then needs DNS → Edit and Cloudflare Tunnel → Edit. Every change lands in the audit log.
